messages:
Alice S.: bump — ACME support ticket just escalated. After tonight's rollout (redwood-v2-7b:v2.2) they report responses that include stale customer-specific prefixes/templates from the previous model variant. Behaves like KV/prefix cache wasn't invalidated on the rollout. They say some answers reference old onboarding text (which contains internal placeholders). Clearly bad.

Alice S.: repro steps I used (from their report):
1) POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
2) headers: Authorization: Bearer <ACME-KEY>
3) body: {
  "model": "redwood-v2-7b",
  "model_version": "v2.2",
  "prompt": "<customer_prefix>
User: what is my onboarding date?
Assistant:",
  "stream": false
}

Alice S.: sample response (trimmed):
"Assistant: Your onboarding was on 02/04/2024. Also, remember to use internal-XXXX for ..."
-> That internal bit matches the old prefix used by a different tenant during earlier eval runs. They attached request_id: rq_3f9b2a and region: us-west-2.

Sam O.: :eyes: thanks. Do we have the serving node / trace id? Can we see which cache key hit? If it's KV cache, we'd expect key composition to include model_version, but maybe we changed the key format and left stale entries.

Alice S.: I asked customer for the full headers; they sent back trace: trace: tr_202c9f, request_id: rq_3f9b2a. They also included a small chronology: old responses started appearing ~20m after canary reached 50% traffic.

Maria R.: copying in runtime. Quick hypothesis: when we rolled to v2.2 we changed prompt-normalization logic (prefix normalization), but didn't bump the cache namespace. If cache keys are computed as sha(prefix) without including a model variant salt, then old cached KV entries could be served to new model variant when the runtime reuses the same cache bucket.

Maria R.: can you grab the serving logs for tr_202c9f? Use this query on Loki/ELK: 
``` 
{job="redwood-serving", region="us-west-2", trace_id="tr_202c9f"} |= "cache-hit" | json
```

ops-bot: deploy-canary-redwood-v2-7b:v2.2 @ 2026-03-14T22:10:03Z :pushpin: deploy id dpl_77a2c

Lee I.: I just checked the canary deploy logs. Canary finished & marked healthy at 22:30 but we rotated the inference cache worker pool at 22:25. If cache worker restart reused existing backing store without flushing, that lines up.

Lee I.: quick mitigation — we can invalidate prefix/KV cache keys for v2.2 in us-west-2. Command (admin):
``` 
redwood-admin cache invalidate --region us-west-2 --namespace prefix_cache --match "model:redwood-v2-7b:prefix:*" --reason "post-deploy prefix mismatch"
```

Maria R.: also add a safer invalidation script to the deploy pipeline that runs when prompt-normalization or prefix format changes. For now, manual invalidate then monitor ACME traffic.

Tess H.: I'm drafting a customer response. Tentative message: "Thanks for flagging — we believe cached prefix data from a prior variant was served after a recent rollout. We're invalidating the relevant cache entries and will monitor. We'll follow up with a root cause and steps taken." Want to confirm before I send.

Jordan P.: please include a temporary credit for ACME while this is resolved. Also log this as a regression in the rollout playbook. Action items: (1) fix cache-key to include model_version salt, (2) add post-deploy cache sanity checks, (3) add e2e test to catch cross-tenant prefix bleed.

Sam O.: agree. Also add an alert when a single tenant's responses change content hash by >X% after rollout (we can use prompt families to detect).

Alice S.: running the invalidate now (will paste output). If this doesn't clear it we'll rollback canary in that region.

Alice S.: (run output)
``` 
$ redwood-admin cache invalidate --region us-west-2 --namespace prefix_cache --match "model:redwood-v2-7b:prefix:*" --reason "post-deploy prefix mismatch"
Invalidation submitted: job_id inv_8b3d
Affected keys approx: 12,438
Status: queued -> completed
```

Lee I.: invalidation completed and propagation shows TTL=0 now. Please repro with the original request id.

Alice S.: re-tested with customer's exact payload + key: request_id rq_3f9b2a variant -> now response does NOT include internal-XXXX. Sending update to ACME, include incident id INC-2026-0314-1.

Tess H.: Sent to customer: "We invalidated cached prefix entries and verified responses returning to expected behavior. We're performing a deeper postmortem and will share remediation steps by EOD." Customer replied: "Thanks, looks ok so far. Please confirm root cause." They want a timeline.

Maria R.: Will lead the postmortem. Root cause summary for customer: prefix cache keys didn't include a model variant namespace; prompt-normalization tweak changed prefix fingerprints enabling cross-variant reuse. Remediation: bump cache key to include model_version, add deploy-time cache invalidation when prompt/prefix format changes, & add regression tests.

Jordan P.: add this to the rollout checklist and mark blocker for next deploy until cache-key fix is live. Assign to infra/runtime.

Alice S.: I'll keep monitoring ACME for 24h, will escalate to rollback if recurrence. Thanks all for quick triage. :thumbsup:

Sam O.: filing follow-up issues: ENG-1279 (cache-key fix), ENG-1280 (deploy invalidation), SUPPORT-432 (customer credits/comms). I'll add owners.

Alice S.: closing thread for now — will update last_message_ts when postmortem draft ready."
